note: Declared normalizations for scripts/emit_diff.py -- the golden-emit differ used to
prove the Quartz replacement emits the same site.
THE RULE ABOUT RULES. This list starts EMPTY and stays empty until a difference has
actually been OBSERVED between two builds of identical source. A rule written from a
guess ('timestamps probably vary') is how a real regression hides: it forgives a whole
field forever in exchange for a convenience nobody measured. Over-normalizing is the
single failure this file exists to prevent.
To earn a row you need all four of:
id        a greppable handle
field     a regex matched against the FULL field path emit_diff.py prints
reason    why the value differs between two builds of identical source
evidence  the run that showed it -- a determinism probe, with the observed counts
and optionally `path`, a regex scoping the rule to some files.
emit_diff.py prints how many differences each rule suppressed, and EXITS 2 when a rule
suppresses zero. A rule that matches nothing has rotted: either the volatility it was
written for is gone, or the field was renamed and the rule is now silently forgiving
nothing while looking like coverage. Same failure the ruleset_surfaces.json gate
catches for enumerations.
NOT NORMALIZATIONS, AND DO NOT ADD THEM HERE. These are inputs to be HELD CONSTANT
between golden and candidate, which scripts/emit_golden.sh records into <label>.env.txt:
POSTHOG_API_KEY / POSTHOG_API_HOST / SUPABASE_URL / SUPABASE_ANON_KEY  (quartz.config.ts,
via dotenv/config resolved against source/, where there is no .env)
AFFILIATE_REF      (scripts/apply_affiliate_ref.py -- unset leaves links neutral)
SHOW_BREADCRUMBS   (quartz.layout.ts -- unset drops the Breadcrumbs component)
the CHECKOUT ITSELF: article:published_time / JSON-LD datePublished / sitemap <lastmod>
all derive from fileData.dates.created, which is the source file's filesystem
BIRTHTIME (quartz/plugins/transformers/lastmod.ts -- the 'git' source supplies only
`modified`, never `created`, so `created` always falls through to st.birthtimeMs).
In a fresh git worktree that is the checkout time, so it is identical for every build
IN one worktree and different between two worktrees. The correct handling is to run
golden and candidate in the SAME worktree, not to normalize the field -- normalizing
it would also forgive an emitter that dropped datePublished altogether.
